items.description: Attackers are actively exploiting vulnerabilities across critical network infrastructure, and PHP flaws known as "PHP2Shell" put the web management interfaces of firewalls, VPNs, application delivery controllers, and other appliances at risk. [...]

items.title: Even after PHP2Shell, blast radius matters more than a CVSS score
items.description: PHP2Shell shows how quickly attackers can exploit critical vulnerabilities, often before organizations have time to patch. Token Security explains why limiting the access of service accounts, API keys, and AI agents is just as important as fixing vulnerabilities to reduce the damage from a breach. [...]

items.description: Google released a Chrome security update that fixes 52 vulnerabilities, including four critical flaws affecting FileSystem, FileAPI, Skia, and Layout. According to the release notice, the Stable channel is moving to version 156.0.8078.73/.74 for Windows and Mac. At the same time, Linux users will receive version 156.0.8078.73. items.title: FBI Seizes Virtualine Bulletproof Hosting Domain Linked to Ransomware and Cybercrime
items.description: The FBI seized virtualine.net, the main website of a bulletproof hosting provider linked to ransomware operators, stolen-data markets, and other cybercrime services. items.title: Chrome and Firefox Updates Patch Over 200 Vulnerabilities
items.description: The Chrome 156 update fixes 52 bugs, while Firefox 159 was rolled out with 167 security patches. The post Chrome and Firefox Updates Patch Over 200 Vulnerabilities appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: Malicious Firefox Extensions Impersonate Phantom, Jupiter, and Bitget to Steal Crypto Wallet Keys
items.description: Three malicious Firefox extensions posed as the Phantom, Jupiter, and Bitget crypto wallets to steal recovery phrases and private keys. Whoever holds these secrets controls the wallet and every coin in it. All three listings were live on the Firefox Add-ons store during the research and have since been removed. items.title: TLS Flaws Found in GoAhead Web Server Used in Hundreds of Millions of Devices
items.description: FoxIO disclosed three GoAhead TLS bugs that can let revoked certificates through or expose some encrypted sessions to eavesdroppers. The post TLS Flaws Found in GoAhead Web Server Used in Hundreds of Millions of Devices appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: Hackers Use Fake Court Notices to Deliver XWorm Malware Through Hidden Windows Scripts
items.description: Attackers are sending fake court notices to organizations in Colombia and using them to install XWorm, a remote access tool that gives criminals full control of an infected PC. The emails look like real legal letters. The attached files are hidden Windows scripts that quietly start the infection. items.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit PHP2Shell to Root Firewalls
items.description: The attackers chained PHP2Shell and Fragnesia exploits and hacked two servers of a US government-affiliated organization. The post China-Linked Hackers Exploit PHP2Shell to Root Firewalls appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.description: A critical 16-year-old flaw in EDK II, the open-source code that most hardware makers use to build UEFI firmware, can allow an attacker to run code on a machine before its operating system loads, but only while the machine is booting over the network. items.description: Adobe has released patches to address multiple critical security flaws in Campaign Classic that, if successfully exploited, could result in arbitrary code execution, security feature bypass, and privilege escalation. The list of eight vulnerabilities is as follows - CVE-2026-104351 (CVSS score: 9.9) - A code injection vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution.
